title: Generic fibre ranks and admissible invariance of the affine flattening hypotheses
statement: Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, $f:X\to S$ an affine flat morphism of finite presentation, and $\mathcal F$ a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. Suppose every fibre is geometrically integral, meaning integral after every field extension. Let $U\subset S$ be a quasi-compact open such that $\mathcal F|_{X_U}$ is of finite presentation and $\mathcal F$ is flat over $S$ at every fibre generic point over $U$. For $u\in U$ write $\xi_u$ for the unique generic point of $X_u$ and set $r(u)=\dim_{\kappa(\xi_u)}(\mathcal F_{\xi_u}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,\xi_u}}\kappa(\xi_u))$. Then $\mathcal F$ is free of rank $r(u)$ on an open neighbourhood of $\xi_u$ in $X_U$, and $r:U\to\mathbf N$ is locally constant. Its nonempty level sets give a finite partition $U=\coprod_{i\in I}U_i$ into quasi-compact clopen opens. Moreover, after any finite sequence of admissible blowups with respect to the successive inverse images of $U$, the transformed base is quasi-compact and quasi-separated; the base-changed family is affine, flat, of finite presentation, with geometrically integral fibres; and the successive module strict transform is quasi-coherent of finite type. Over the inverse image of $U$ it identifies with $\mathcal F|_{X_U}$, is of finite presentation, and is free at the fibre generic points with the same ranks $r(u)$. Admissible blowups and module strict transform retain their centres as in [def-nagata-admissible-blowup], [def-trf-module-strict-transform]. Schemes, morphism properties, quasi-coherent modules, finite type and finite presentation, relative module flatness, integral schemes, fibres, generic points and residue fields are as in [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-pc-scheme-fibre], [def-sc-generic-point], [def-weil-residue-field].

proof.text: Fix $u\in U$. The integral fibre $X_u$ is nonempty and irreducible by [def-pc-integral-scheme], and has a unique generic point $\xi_u$ by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. Choose a nonempty affine open in $X_u$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], $\mathcal O_{X_u,\xi_u}$ is a field. Consequently $(\mathcal F_u)_{\xi_u}$ is flat over that field by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat]. The morphism $X_U\to U$ is of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). The module $\mathcal F|_{X_U}$ is finitely presented by hypothesis, and its stalk at $\xi_u$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{U,u}$ by the assumed relative flatness. Thus [lem-trf-flat-fibre-free-neighbourhood] gives an open $W_u\subset X_U$ containing $\xi_u$ and an isomorphism $\mathcal F|_{W_u}\cong\mathcal O_{W_u}^{\oplus n_u}$. Taking the stalk and then tensoring with $\kappa(\xi_u)$ sends the standard basis to a basis of $\kappa(\xi_u)^{\oplus n_u}$, so $n_u=r(u)$, including when $n_u=0$.

source.place: Tag 0811, lemma-flatten-module-pre, rank paragraph; more-morphisms.tex Tag 080Q, lemma-flat-and-free-at-point-fibre, with its preceding explanation about reduced fibre generic points

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open], $f$ is open. Therefore $V_u=f(W_u)$ is an open neighbourhood of $u$ contained in $U$. If $v\in V_u$, then $W_u\cap X_v$ is a nonempty open subset of the integral fibre $X_v$, so it contains $\xi_v$: every open meeting the closure of a generic point contains that point. The same trivialization on $W_u$ now gives $\mathcal F_{\xi_v}\otimes\kappa(\xi_v)\cong\kappa(\xi_v)^{\oplus r(u)}$. Its standard basis shows $r(v)=r(u)$. These $V_u$ prove local constancy of $r$.

source.place: Tag 0811, lemma-flatten-module-pre, rank paragraph; morphisms.tex Tag 01UA, lemma-fppf-open

proof.text: For each $i\in\mathbf N$ put $U_i=\{u\in U:r(u)=i\}$. Local constancy makes $U_i$ open, and its complement, the union of the other level sets, is open too. The nonempty $U_i$ form a disjoint open cover of the quasi-compact space $U$. A finite subcover therefore contains all nonempty level sets. Each is closed in $U$, hence quasi-compact: add its open complement to any open cover and use quasi-compactness of $U$. This gives the asserted finite partition into quasi-compact clopen opens. For $U=\varnothing$ the index set is empty.

source.place: Tag 0811, lemma-flatten-module-pre, rank paragraph, finite open-and-closed partition

proof.text: For any morphism $g:T\to S$, write $f_T:X_T\to T$ for the second projection. It is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1), flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], and of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). For $t\in T$ and $s=g(t)$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-of-base-change] identifies $(X_T)_t$ with $X_s\times_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(t)$. If $L/\kappa(t)$ is any field extension, the defining universal property of fibre products identifies its further extension with $X_s\times_{\kappa(s)}L$: on test schemes both are the same compatible maps to $X_s$ and $\operatorname{Spec}L$. This is integral by the original geometric integrality hypothesis applied to the composite field extension $L/\kappa(s)$. Thus the base-changed family again has geometrically integral fibres.

source.place: Tag 0811, lemma-flatten-module-pre, preservation of hypotheses in first proof paragraph; morphisms.tex Tags 01SD (lemma-base-change-affine), 01U9 (lemma-base-change-flat), 01TS (lemma-base-change-finite-presentation)

proof.text: Take one $U$-admissible blowup $b:S_1\to S$ with its specified centre. By [lem-trf-module-admissible-blowup-calculus](2), $S_1$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and the module strict transform $\mathcal F_1$ on $X\times_SS_1$ is quasi-coherent and of finite type. By [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open] the restriction $b^{-1}U\to U$ is the specified isomorphism. In particular $b^{-1}U$ is quasi-compact. Under this isomorphism and the induced isomorphism $X\times_S b^{-1}U\cong X_U$, the agreement-over-$U$ clause of [lem-trf-module-admissible-blowup-calculus](2) identifies $\mathcal F_1$ with $\mathcal F|_{X_U}$. Hence its finite presentation there is unchanged. The same identification takes each fibre and its unique generic point over $u$ to $X_u$ and $\xi_u$, and takes its stalk and residue field to the original ones. Restricting the trivializations of Step 1 along this isomorphism gives the claimed free neighbourhoods and the identical ranks $r(u)$.

source.place: Tag 080Y, remark-successive-blowups; divisors.tex Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform, and the preservation of the open complement of a blowup centre

proof.text: Induct on the sequence length. For length zero all assertions are the hypotheses and Steps 1--3. Suppose they hold on $S_j$, with $U^{(j)}$ the inverse image of $U$, $X_j=X\times_SS_j$ and $\mathcal F_j$ the successive strict transform. The induction hypothesis makes $S_j$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $U^{(j)}$ quasi-compact, and $\mathcal F_j$ quasi-coherent of finite type. Thus [lem-trf-module-admissible-blowup-calculus](2) applies to the next $U^{(j)}$-admissible blowup, retaining its actual centre, and gives these same properties on $S_{j+1}$. Step 4 applied to $X_j\to S_j$ gives all family properties after this base change. The isomorphism-over-the-open statement [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open] and the agreement of strict transforms over that open identify the new restricted module with the previous one, and hence with $\mathcal F|_{X_U}$. The restricted finite presentation, relative flatness at fibre generic points, free neighbourhoods and ranks are therefore exactly the original ones. This proves the induction and every asserted invariance for any finite sequence.
